npcs.name: Tilda Hael
npcs.idle: If you see a fisherman with a mole shaped like a crown, kindly drag him home by the ear.

npcs.name: Marsh-Warden Brec
npcs.idle: Bogmen don't hurt you if you don't hurt them. Mostly.

npcs.name: Squire Hamon
npcs.idle: My knight died in the north marsh. A squire without a knight is just a boy with a sword.

npcs.name: Sir Baldwin the Elder
npcs.idle: I was a knight of the Vigil once. Long before they drowned.

npcs.name: Warden-Captain Maelor
npcs.idle: Adribard's Retreat is dry, mostly. That's the best I can say for it.

npcs.name: Lady Argante
npcs.idle: Three queens carried the King across that water. I was there. I keep the shore.

quests.title: The Bog King
quests.offer:
My Dai is a fisherman, and a poor one, and the gentlest man in Avalon. Three days ago the bogmen came and took him off in his own boat - singing! - and they bowed to him.

He's got a birthmark like a little crown. The Warden says that's why. Will you [bring Dai home]? Brec the [warden] knows where they've taken him.
quests.summary: Bogmen carried off Tilda Hael's betrothed, a fisherman with a crown-shaped birthmark, and bowed to him.

steps.goal: Ask the marsh-warden about the bogmen
steps.say: Crown-mark, eh? The bogmen have a story about a king who'll come out of the water marked like that. They've been waiting a long while. They'll have him at the bog [towers] in the south.

steps.goal: Get past the bogman gatherers
steps.text: They fight half-heartedly and keep looking south, towards the towers, as if afraid you'll interrupt something.

steps.goal: Find Dai at the bog towers
steps.text: Dai Morrow sits on a throne of reeds and driftwood, wearing a crown of lilies, eating something unidentifiable from a shell. He looks happier than any man you've ever seen.

steps.goal: Talk to Dai Morrow
steps.say:
Oh! Hello! Did Tilda send you? She would. Isn't this mad?

They bow to me. They bring me fish - good fish, better than I ever caught. They listen when I talk. Nobody's ever listened when I talk. I've never been [anything], you understand. Here I'm a king.

steps.goal: Decide what Dai should do
steps.say:
Tilda's a good woman. Too good for me, everybody said so. Maybe she'd be better off.

I don't know. You tell me. [Come home], or [stay] here and be a king of frogs and mud. I'll do whatever you say. I always do whatever people say. Except here.

options.say: Right. Yes. Home. They won't like it - hold on, they REALLY won't like it -
Really? You think so? Then tell Tilda... tell her I'm sorry. And I'm happy. Both at once. Is that allowed?

steps.goal: Get Dai out of the bog
steps.text: The bogmen fall back into the water. Dai takes his crown off, looks at it, and puts it in his pocket.

stages.name: Keep Dai alive
stages.announce: The bogmen howl. 'The king is leaving! The king is leaving!'
stages.thanks: That was horrible. I'm keeping the crown.

stages.name: Bog-Mother Sloe
stages.announce: A huge old bogwoman rises out of the mere. 'MY king. MINE. Leave him!'

steps.goal: Bring Dai home to Tilda
steps.say:
DAI MORROW. You absolute -

He's asleep. He kept the crown, the fool. He says they listened to him. I listen to him! I'll listen better. Here, take something, before I cry.

steps.goal: Tell Tilda Hael
steps.say:
He's... staying. As a king. Of the bogmen.

You know, I always knew he'd leave me. I just thought it'd be for a woman. Not for - frogs. Take this. It was meant for him.

quests.title: Until Relieved
quests.offer:
My knight, Sir Corentin, led a patrol into the north marsh to find the old Order of the Vigil. They held these marshes three hundred years ago and drowned in them, still at their posts. Corentin found them. They killed him.

I want to finish what he started. Old Sir [Baldwin] in the abbey town knows the Vigil's story. Will you [help me]?

topics.Baldwin: Sir Baldwin the Elder, in the abbey town east. He's ancient. He was a squire of the Vigil, if you can believe it.

quests.summary: Squire Hamon's knight died seeking the drowned Order of the Vigil in the north marsh.

steps.goal: Ask old Sir Baldwin about the Vigil
steps.say: The Vigil? Gods, I haven't heard that name in fifty years. I was the last squire they took before the marsh rose. They swore to hold the north marsh 'until relieved'. Nobody came to relieve them. The war moved on, and they drowned still standing their [watch].

steps.goal: Go into the north marsh
steps.text: Torches burn on poles in the water. Figures in rotten plate stand guard at every one.

steps.goal: Break through the Vigil's footmen
Find Sir Corentin
steps.text: Sir Corentin lies with his sword still in hand and three dead ghouls around him. He died well. His signet is still on his finger.

steps.goal: Defeat the Ghoul Lord of the Vigil
steps.text: The Ghoul Lord kneels in the water. 'Are you... our relief?'

stages.name: Lord-Commander of the Vigil
stages.announce: A great ghoul in a captain's plate raises a black sword. 'HALT. None pass the Vigil.'

steps.goal: Speak to the last knight of the Vigil
steps.say:
Three hundred years at our posts. We could not leave. We are sworn, until relieved.

You could speak the words - Sir Baldwin will have taught the squire, and the squire you. 'I relieve you.' Then we sleep. Or take our [banner] to Camelot, so they remember we held. But then we stand here until someone else comes.

Will you [relieve us]?

options.say: ...Relieved. Relieved. Thank you. Thank you. Watch - watch is - ended.
Take it. Let them know. We will hold. We have always held.

steps.goal: Return to Squire Hamon
steps.say:
You relieved them? All of them? Sir Corentin would've - he'd have wept. He was soft like that.

I'll take his signet to his mother. And then I suppose I'll find another knight. Here - from his things.

steps.goal: Return to Squire Hamon
steps.say:
The banner of the Vigil. In Camelot. Sir Corentin would have been proud.

...They're still standing there, though. Aren't they. Still holding. Waiting. Here - from his things.

quests.title: The Bogmen's Nets
quests.offer:
Bogmen. Usually they keep to themselves and their fish. This month they've been stringing nets across the channels south of the Retreat and taking whoever paddles into them.

Will you [cut the nets]? Thin the bogmen while you're at it.
quests.summary: Bogmen are stringing nets across the channels south of Adribard's Retreat.

steps.goal: Drive off the bogmen in the channels about 160 m south-west of Warden-Captain Maelor
Cut the bogmen's nets

clue.name: a net strung across the channel

steps.text: You cut the nets. Tangled in one: a little crown of reeds, the kind the bogmen weave for someone they bow to.

steps.goal: Tell Warden-Captain Maelor
steps.say: A reed crown. They've got a king again, have they? Tilda Hael in Caer Witrin had trouble with that.

quests.title: The Drowned Church
quests.offer:
There was a church in the middle marsh once - the marsh ate it a hundred years ago. Its dead have started walking: bloody-bones, the locals call the worst of them.

Will you [put them down]?
quests.summary: The dead of a drowned church walk the middle marsh.

steps.goal: Put down the bloody-bones about 630 m south-west of Warden-Captain Maelor
Lay the decayed dead to rest
Tell Warden-Captain Maelor
steps.say: The marsh is restless. The Lady on the shore says it's because of who's been crossing to the Isle.

quests.title: Lights over the Water
quests.offer:
Will o' wisps over the south pools. They lead fishermen out onto soft ground and leave them there.

Will you [put out the lights]? Kill enough and the rest go dim.
quests.summary: Will o' wisps lead fishermen to their deaths in the south pools.

steps.goal: Put out the will o' wisps about 590 m south of Marsh-Warden Brec
Tell Warden Brec
steps.say: Quieter nights for the fishermen. Thank you.

quests.title: Scrags in the Reeds
quests.offer:
Scrags in the southern reeds, and a big one called Scraek in the middle marsh who leads them. They've started raiding the fishing huts.

Will you [deal with the scrags]?
quests.summary: Scrags led by Scraek are raiding the fishing huts in the south.

steps.goal: Clear the scrags in the southern reeds about 790 m south-east of Marsh-Warden Brec
Kill Scraek
Tell Warden Brec
steps.say: Scraek, dead? The fishermen will name a boat after you.

quests.title: The Thickening Mist
quests.offer:
The mist round the Isle has thickened, and the sprites in it have turned sharp. The mist is the Isle's guard - it only thickens when someone tries to cross who shouldn't.

Will you [walk the shore]? Thin the sprites, and look at the landing.

topics.queens: Three queens took Arthur to Avalon in the black barge: the Queen of Northgales, the Queen of the Waste Lands - and Morgan le Fay. Yes. She was one of them. That is what frightens me.

quests.summary: The mist round the Isle of Avalon has thickened, which means someone is trying to cross.

steps.goal: Thin the mist sprites about 160 m west of Lady Argante
Search the landing on the Isle's shore
steps.text: Keel-marks in the mud, fresh. A long, narrow boat has been drawn up here - and the rope-post is tied with a red cord.

steps.goal: Tell Lady Argante
steps.say:
A long, narrow boat. There is only one boat that crosses to the Isle, and it is black, and it carried the King.

Someone is using the barge.

default.text: From the Keepers of the Isle.

quests.title: The Black Barge
quests.offer:
The barge is rowed by the dead of the shore chapel - the knights and pages who kept vigil for the King and drowned at their posts. They row for the Keepers. But they're rowing for someone else now.

Will you [go to the chapel]? Find out who they row for.
quests.summary: The black barge that carried Arthur to Avalon is being rowed for someone else by the dead of the shore chapel.

steps.goal: Get past the phantom pages about 610 m south-east of Lady Argante
Read the shore chapel's register

clue.name: a register in the chapel's ruin

steps.text: The last pages, in a new hand: 'The barge goes out at the new moon for whoever bears the key and the crown, by order of the Lady of the Lake's sister.' And a list of crossings - eleven of them.

steps.goal: Bring the register to Lady Argante
steps.say:
'The Lady of the Lake's sister.' Morgana has bound the barge's dead to her seal. Eleven crossings. Eleven of her people have stood on the Isle where the King sleeps.

God help us if one of them reaches him.

default.text: From the Keepers of the Isle.

quests.title: The Fallen Paladins
quests.offer:
The barge's dead won't stop rowing while their captains hold them to Morgana's seal: Sir Fiedel and the Dread Lord Aryon, who were paladins of the King once. They fell when the vigil drowned and got up again under her hand.

Will you [free the chapel]? Bring your strongest. They were the best of us.
quests.summary: Two fallen paladins hold the dead of the shore chapel to Morgana's seal.

steps.goal: Cut through the ghostly knights at the shore chapel about 730 m south of Lady Argante
Defeat Undead Knight Fiedel
Defeat Dread Lord Aryon
steps.text: Aryon kneels in the water. 'Tell the King,' he says, 'we kept the vigil as long as we could.'

steps.goal: Tell Lady Argante
steps.say:
They're free. The barge will row for the Keepers again, and only for us.

I'll tell the King myself, when he wakes. He'll want to know.

default.text: From the Keepers of the Isle.

quests.title: The Shambling Road
quests.offer:
Shamblers in the south-west - walking heaps of marsh. They've always been there. But now they walk in lines, and they carry things.

Will you [follow the shamblers]?
quests.summary: The shamblers of the south-west marsh walk in lines, carrying things.

steps.goal: Break up the shambler lines about 230 m south-west of Marsh-Warden Brec
Look at what the shamblers carried
steps.text: Blocks of grey granite flecked with pink, dressed square. The shamblers were carrying them east, toward the Isle.

steps.goal: Tell Warden Brec
steps.say: Granite? We've no granite in the marsh. That's Cornwall's - or further.

quests.title: Wolves of the West Marsh
quests.offer:
Giant wolves on the west marsh - out of Cornwall, I'd guess, driven ahead of something bigger. They've taken two of my wardens.

Will you [hunt the wolves]?
quests.summary: Giant wolves, driven out of Cornwall, are hunting the west marsh.

steps.goal: Hunt the giant wolves about 310 m north-west of Marsh-Warden Brec
Tell Warden Brec
steps.say: Driven ahead of something bigger. I keep coming back to that.

quests.title: What Walks in the Fog
quests.offer:
On the far west marsh the fog never lifts, and something walks in it. Mist monsters, the old fishermen say. Nobody who goes in to look comes back to say more.

Will you [go into the fog]? Bring friends who can find you.
quests.summary: Mist monsters walk the fog of the far west marsh.

steps.goal: Kill the mist monsters about 1.2 km west of Warden-Captain Maelor
Tell Warden-Captain Maelor
steps.say:
You came back. That's more than most. What did you see?

...Giants' footprints, going east. In the fog. Of course.

quests.title: The Giants' Causeway
quests.offer:
My wardens found it in the south-west: a road, of dressed granite, laid across the marsh. Built by giants - Cornish giants, out of the west. And it points at the Isle.

Will you [break the causeway]? Kill the builders. Tip the stones into the mire.
quests.summary: Cornish giants are laying a granite causeway across the south-west marsh toward the Isle.

steps.goal: Kill the giants building the causeway about 280 m south-west of Marsh-Warden Brec
Tip the causeway's kerb-stones into the mire
steps.text: The stone goes over with a heave and a sucking splash. Carved on its underside: a dragon's claw, and 'For the Sleeper.'

steps.goal: Tell Warden Brec
steps.say:
'For the Sleeper.' A road to the King, so the giants can walk to him dry-shod.

The Lady on the shore must hear this.

quests.title: The Marsh Lord
quests.offer:
The giants couldn't lay a road through the mire without the mire's leave. The Marsh Lord gave it - the old thing that rules the deep bog in the far south-west. The bogmen whisper he was paid in Cornish tin.

Will you [end the Marsh Lord]? He's old and he's strong. Take everyone.
quests.summary: The Marsh Lord sold the giants the way across the mire for Cornish tin.

steps.goal: Break the mud golems that guard the mire road about 160 m east of Marsh-Warden Brec
Defeat the Marsh Lord
steps.text: The Marsh Lord sinks into his bog with a long, wet sigh. Tin ingots tumble out of the mud where he lay.

steps.goal: Tell Warden Brec
steps.say:
Tin. He sold the King's marsh for tin.

Without him, the mire won't hold their road. You've bought the Isle time.

quests.title: The Ghoul Court
quests.offer:
The Vigil's dead hold court in the north-west marsh - ghoul footmen drilling on the old parade ground as if nothing's changed in three hundred years.

I want to know what they're guarding. Will you [scout the court]?
quests.summary: The Drowned Vigil's ghoul footmen drill on their old parade ground in the north-west.

steps.goal: Fight through the ghoul footmen about 580 m west of Squire Hamon
Search the Vigil's walls
steps.text: Behind the walls, the Vigil's keep - and on its tower, still flying after three hundred years, a banner. Grey, with a white tower. The Vigil's colours.

steps.goal: Tell Squire Hamon
steps.say:
Their banner still flies. Sir Corentin would have given anything to see it.

If we could take it down - take the keep back - the Vigil could rest.

quests.title: The Vigil's Banner
quests.offer:
The Vigil drowned at its posts because nobody came to relieve them. Somebody should. Bring down their banner from the keep, and they'll know they've been relieved.

Will you [bring down the banner]? The keep is full of them. You'll need a group.
quests.summary: Squire Hamon wants the Drowned Vigil's banner brought down from their keep, so they know they've been relieved.

steps.goal: Cut through the ghoul knights in the keep about 580 m west of Squire Hamon
Defeat a ghoul lord of the Vigil
Bring down the banner from the tower
steps.text: The banner comes down in your hands, damp and heavy. Across the keep, for a moment, every ghoul stands still and looks up.

steps.goal: Bring the banner to Squire Hamon
steps.say:
Relieved. After three hundred years.

They won't all rest yet - they're too used to standing. But the Marsh Wardens could take that keep now, with enough hands.

quests.title: The Way to the Isle
quests.offer:
The barge is free and the causeway's broken - and that has made her angry. Morgause of Orkney is coming to the shore herself: Morgana's sister, Mordred's mother. She'll try to cross by force.

Will you [stand on the shore] with me? Bring everyone. This is the King's last door.
quests.summary: Morgause of Orkney, Morgana's sister, comes to force a crossing to the Isle where Arthur sleeps.

steps.goal: Go to the Isle's landing about 140 m east of Lady Argante
steps.text: The mist parts. Red torches on the water, coming closer.

steps.goal: Keep Lady Argante alive on the landing
steps.text: The Crimson break on the shore - and a tall woman in a black crown steps out of the mist.

stages.name: Keep Lady Argante alive
stages.announce: Argante raises her hands and the mist thickens round the landing. 'Hold them! They must not set foot on the Isle!'

stages.name: Morgause of Orkney
stages.announce: Morgause of Orkney, in a black crown: 'My son is dead because of that man. Let me see him sleep. Only for a moment.'

steps.goal: Speak with Lady Argante on the shore
steps.say:
She's gone - back into the mist. Not dead. Her kind never quite are.

The King sleeps safe tonight. But his enemies know the way now: Morgana at the lake of Llyn Barfog, and the white dragon in Dartmoor. Shall I [ring the shore-bell], so every Keeper and Warden knows the Isle held? Or do we [keep it quiet], and let them wonder?

options.say: Then ring it. Let them hear it in Camelot.
Then the Isle keeps its own counsel, as it always has.

rung.text: From the Keepers of the Isle.

quiet.text: From the Keepers of the Isle.
